newsitem.title: GERMANY: German IBIS DAX ends strongly ahead, lifted by U.S.
newsitem.headline: German IBIS DAX ends strongly ahead, lifted by U.S.

text.p: German shares advanced strongly in volatile afternoon electronic trade, boosted by lower-than-expected U.S. consumer prices data which led to a strong opening on the Dow Jones Industrial index on Wall Street.

The IBIS DAX index, which tracks electronic trade in German blue -chips, ended the day up 2.18 percent at 3,369.26 points, a rise of 71.74 points. Its bourse trade counterpart, the DAX index, ended trade earlier at 3,327.68 points, up 1.46 percent or 47.78 points.

"The U.S. consumer prices data was encouraging but nobody should go mega-bullish on it. It was a relief to the nervousness which has been around since last Friday and there is support coming from the firm dollar and stronger Bunds," a share trader said.
The Dow Jones Industrials Index was up well over one percent at 6,527.36 points in early trade, rising on the back of lower-than-expected consumer prices in the U.S.

Consumer prices rose 0.1 percent in March compared with forecasts that it would rise 0.2 percent, while core CPI rose 0.2 percent versus the 0.3 percent forecast, which served to calm fears of trans-Atlantic inflationary pressure.

"A lot of trade at the moment is options-driven, which means people are shying away from the market because it is not really representative of the way things are going in the market," the trader said.
Carmaker Volkswagen AG also yo-yoed over the day, trading in a range between 1,033.50 marks and 1,076 marks. "This is indicative of the kind of volatility we are seeing today," the trader said.
Volkswagen shares ended at 1,056.50 marks, up 6.70 marks, in late IBIS trade.
In such an unpredictable market, market players were hesitant to make any firm forecasts for the rest of the week.
"We're only really as good as the next set of figures," said one trader.
